title: The Chain: Lagrange → Orbit-Stabilizer → Burnside
content:
Three fundamental results in group theory form a logical chain:

$$\text{Lagrange} \xrightarrow{\text{generalizes}} \text{Orbit-Stabilizer} \xrightarrow{\text{derives}} \text{Burnside}$$

**Lagrange (1771)**: $|H| \mid |G|$ for any subgroup $H \leq G$.

**Orbit-Stabilizer**: For any group action of $G$ on $X$ and $x \in X$: $|\text{Orb}(x)| \cdot |\text{Stab}(x)| = |G|$.

**Burnside (Cauchy-Frobenius)**: $|X/G| = \frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} |\text{Fix}(g)|$.

All three are in Mathlib; this file formalizes the chain explicitly.
mathContext: Lagrange proves $|G| = [G:H] \cdot |H|$ by showing cosets partition $G$ into $[G:H]$ equal parts of size $|H|$. Orbit-stabilizer IS Lagrange applied to $\text{Stab}(x) \leq G$: since $\text{Orb}(x) \cong G/\text{Stab}(x)$, we get $|\text{Orb}(x)| = [G:\text{Stab}(x)] = |G|/|\text{Stab}(x)|$. Burnside derives from orbit-stabilizer via double counting: $\sum_{g \in G} |\text{Fix}(g)| = |\{(g,x) : g \cdot x = x\}| = \sum_{x \in X} |\text{Stab}(x)| = \sum_{\text{orbits } O} \sum_{x \in O} |\text{Stab}(x)| = \sum_{\text{orbits}} |G| = |X/G| \cdot |G|$, using orbit-stabilizer for $\sum_{x \in O} |\text{Stab}(x)| = |G|$. In Lean: `Mathlib.GroupTheory.GroupAction.Defs` provides `MulAction`, `orbit`, `stabilizer`, `fixedBy`; `Mathlib.GroupTheory.Burnside` provides `sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group`.

title: Lagrange's Theorem in Lean
content:
Two forms of Lagrange's theorem:

1. **Divisibility form** (`lagrange_divides`): $|H| \mid |G|$. One-line proof delegating to `Subgroup.card_subgroup_dvd_card`.

2. **Index form** (`lagrange_index`): $|G| = [G:H] \cdot |H|$. Proof: `(Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup H).symm`.

Both require `[Fintype G]`, `[Fintype H]`, and `[Fintype (G ⧸ H)]` as typeclass instances.
mathContext: `Subgroup.card_subgroup_dvd_card : ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H], Fintype.card H ∣ Fintype.card G` — Mathlib's Lagrange directly. `Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup H : Fintype.card (G ⧸ H) * Fintype.card H = Fintype.card G`; the `.symm` reverses the equation to match `lagrange_index`'s stated form. `G ⧸ H` is the left-coset quotient type: elements are cosets `gH`, and `Fintype.card (G ⧸ H)` computes $[G:H]$. The instance `[Fintype (G ⧸ H)]` requires Lean to know how to enumerate left cosets — it's derivable when `G` and `H` are both `Fintype`. `Fintype.card H ∣ Fintype.card G` is `∃ k, Fintype.card G = Fintype.card H * k`, proved by `k = [G:H]`.

title: Orbit-Stabilizer: Lagrange for Group Actions
content:
Three results formalize orbit-stabilizer:

1. **`orbit_stabilizer`**: $|\text{Orb}(x)| \cdot |\text{Stab}(x)| = |G|$. Proof: `card_orbit_mul_card_stabilizer_eq_card_group G x`.

2. **`orbit_equiv_cosets`**: $\text{Orb}(x) \cong G/\text{Stab}(x)$. Witnesses the bijection via `orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer G x`.

3. **`orbit_stabilizer_generalizes_lagrange`**: Applies orbit-stabilizer to the action $G \curvearrowright G/H$ to recover Lagrange.

The `stabilizer G x : Subgroup G` is a structural subgroup guaranteed by Mathlib.
mathContext: `MulAction.stabilizer G x : Subgroup G` is `{g : G | g • x = x}`, the isotropy group. `MulAction.orbit G x : Set X` is `{g • x | g : G}`. `card_orbit_mul_card_stabilizer_eq_card_group G x : Fintype.card (orbit G x) * Fintype.card (stabilizer G x) = Fintype.card G` — directly from Mathlib's `GroupTheory.GroupAction.Basic`. `orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer G x : orbit G x ≃ G ⧸ stabilizer G x` is the explicit bijection $g \cdot x \mapsto g \cdot \text{Stab}(x)$; it's well-defined because $g_1 x = g_2 x \iff g_2^{-1}g_1 \in \text{Stab}(x) \iff g_1\text{Stab}(x) = g_2\text{Stab}(x)$. `Nonempty (orbit G x ≃ ...)` packages the equivalence propositionally; `⟨orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer G x⟩` is the anonymous constructor. `orbit_stabilizer_generalizes_lagrange` applies Lagrange to the action of $G$ on $G/H$; the stabilizer of the coset $eH$ is $\{g : g \cdot eH = eH\} = \{g : gH = H\} = H$.

title: Burnside's Counting Lemma
content:
**Burnside's lemma** (integer form): $\sum_{g \in G} |\text{Fix}(g)| = |X/G| \cdot |G|$.

```lean
theorem burnside_lemma ... :
    ∑ g : G, Fintype.card (fixedBy X g) =
    Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G X) * Fintype.card G
```

Proof: `sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group G X` (one-line Mathlib delegation).

Divisibility corollary: `rw [burnside_lemma]; exact dvd_mul_left _ _`.
mathContext: `MulAction.fixedBy X g : Set X` is `{x : X | g • x = x}`. `orbitRel.Quotient G X` is the type of orbits — the quotient of $X$ by `orbitRel G X : Setoid X` where `x ~ y ↔ ∃ g, g • x = y`. `sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group : ∑ g : G, Fintype.card (fixedBy X g) = Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G X) * Fintype.card G` — exactly Burnside's lemma in Mathlib. The `[∀ g : G, Fintype (fixedBy X g)]` instance requires each fixed-point set to be finite; this follows from `[Fintype X]` via `Set.fintypeSubset`. `dvd_mul_left a b : a ∣ b * a` closes the divisibility goal after `rw [burnside_lemma]` transforms to `Fintype.card G ∣ Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G X) * Fintype.card G`. Applications: counting distinct necklaces under rotation (Burnside's original problem), distinct colorings of a cube under symmetry group, Polya enumeration theorem (generalization using cycle index).

title: Chain Documentation and open Declarations
content:
**`chain_lagrange_to_burnside`** packages the chain:

```lean
theorem chain_lagrange_to_burnside :
    ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H] [Fintype (G ⧸ H)],
    Fintype.card G = Fintype.card (G ⧸ H) * Fintype.card H :=
  fun H => lagrange_index H
```

This re-states Lagrange but serves as documentation that the chain terminates here.

The `open MulAction Finset BigOperators` at the file top enables `orbit`, `stabilizer`, `fixedBy` (from `MulAction`), `∑` and `∏` notation (from `BigOperators`), and `card`, `sum` etc. (from `Finset`).
mathContext: `chain_lagrange_to_burnside` uses `fun H => lagrange_index H` — a lambda that applies `lagrange_index` to any subgroup. The `[Fintype H]` and `[Fintype (G ⧸ H)]` instance arguments are passed implicitly through `lagrange_index`. The actual mathematical dependency chain inside Mathlib: `burnside_lemma` → `sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group` → `card_orbit_mul_card_stabilizer_eq_card_group` (orbit-stabilizer) → `Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup` (Lagrange). `open BigOperators` is needed because `∑ g : G, ...` is notation from `Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Basic`; without it, you'd write `Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun g => ...)`. `open MulAction` exposes `orbit`, `stabilizer`, `fixedBy`, `orbitRel` without the `MulAction.` prefix. `import Mathlib` gives the entire Mathlib library in one import — the simplest approach for a self-contained demonstration file.
